rows.description: When I feel lonely, the AI chatbot is easy to talk to and never gets tired. That comfort is fine sometimes, but I also need real friends and family; I can tell a trusted person how I feel.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: awe, curiosity, dependence, fear, honesty, trust
related mind states: tiredness, loneliness, trust

rows.description: My teacher asks if I used an AI for my project. I feel tempted to say no. Honestly saying how I used it, and what I did myself, keeps trust and lets her guide me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: awe, curiosity, dependence, fear, loneliness, trust

rows.description: My parent worries about me chatting with AI and asks to see. I feel watched, but sharing openly helps them trust me. I can explain what I use it for and agree on some rules.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: awe, curiosity, dependence, honesty, loneliness, trust

rows.description: The AI writes a poem in seconds and I think it is magic. Wonder is lovely; I also remember it is a tool made by people, and my own imagination is what makes stories mine.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, dependence, fear, honesty, loneliness, trust
related mind states: affection, curiosity, awe

rows.description: An ad shows a cool toy and I suddenly need it. Ads are made to create wanting. I can pause and ask myself if I still want it tomorrow, or if it was just the ad.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, argument, coercion, gratitude

rows.description: A cartoon or celebrity says this snack makes you strong, and I believe it. I learn that ads sell things, so I can ask a parent whether it really is good for me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, argument, coercion, gratitude

rows.description: All my friends have the new branded shoes and I feel left out. Wanting to fit in is human. I can ask myself whether friendship depends on shoes, and talk to my parents honestly.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, argument, gratitude

rows.description: I beg my parents for something I saw in an ad and they refuse. I feel angry and it seems unfair. Understanding their limits and offering to save for it myself shows growing maturity.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, coercion, gratitude

rows.description: I love watching a YouTuber who seems to have a perfect life. Admiration can inspire me, but I remember that videos are edited and nobody's real life is only fun.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, coercion, gratitude
related mind states: playfulness, affection, admiration

rows.description: My parent buys me something after I waited patiently. It feels extra special. Learning to wait makes me value things and understand the effort behind them.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, argument, coercion
